raw:
Saying goodbye to my foster dog. I remember its blanket folded by the front door, and the new owner’s leash on its collar. Those are the things I picture most clearly. A folded blanket is such an ordinary thing, but right then it seemed terribly sad. It was ready to go, and I wasn’t quite ready.

My attention kept going from the blanket to the leash. The leash meant there was somewhere else for the dog to go, a whole life that wouldn’t be with me. I wanted that to be a good thing. Fostering isn’t supposed to mean keeping the dog forever, but knowing that didn’t make the goodbye easy.

I remember feeling attached to all those little familiar things. Even the blanket being folded instead of being used made the leaving feel real.
